questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

assumptions: The currency is euros. get_account and create_promise both use euro cents, so amount_scale is 100 and promise_scale is null (no conversion between the two).
Business days are Monday to Saturday (workdays 0-5). The holidays are 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25.
The brief does not say how to read 'next <weekday>', so the default following_week is used.

Callback days: today, or either of the next two business days (within_business_days:2). Hours are 09:00-18:00 Monday to Friday and 09:00-13:00 Saturday, both ends included. Sunday has no callbacks (window null), callbacks are business days only, and the callback must be later than now.
Callback max_asks is 2. If the person gives an invalid time, the agent proposes one valid time (rule 4). If that is refused too, nothing is booked and the call closes as no_callback.
Identity: one wrong answer is forgiven across the whole check, and the second wrong answer ends it, so max_wrong is 2. This matches the API ('second wrong answer locks the check').

verify_identity returns 'correct' (verified) and 'identity_passed' (all verified). It has no 'wrong answers left' field ('wrong_answers' is a count so far) and no hint field. So response.left and response.hint are empty, hints is empty, and the engine counts wrong answers against max_wrong itself. A value in the wrong format gets ok=false and is not counted.

The year of birth is sent as four digits (kind year, length 4). The customer code is five capital letters or digits with no spaces (upper, length 5). The date of birth is sent as DD.MM.YYYY (%d.%m.%Y), and a date given only as numbers is read day, month, year.
purpose_is_decline keeps the default true because the brief is silent. The brief also says nothing about policy questions, so question_is_decline stays false.

The floor is the card's statement_minimum_cents (floor_field for card). The overdraft has no floor field, so floor_pct=20 with floor_round up_unit applies to it: 20% of amount_due_cents, rounded up to the next whole euro, and an amount that is already a whole euro is not raised. Example: 48735 gives 9747, which becomes 9800; 50000 gives exactly 10000. Credit and overdraft limits are never used.

The brief does not say what happens if the floor is above the amount due. The floor is assumed never to exceed the full amount due (min(floor, full)), because the brief accepts amounts from the floor up to the full amount.
get_account returns one product object under 'account' (not an array). It is read through list_field 'account', with id_field product_id and type_field product_kind.

Bands: early is 1-15 days, deadline the last business day of next week (Monday-Sunday weeks; Saturday counts unless it is a holiday), 1 attempt. Middle is 16-40 days, deadline the 8th business day after today for a card or the 5th for an overdraft, 2 attempts. Late is 41-60 days, deadline the later of the last business day of the month and the 3rd business day after today, 2 attempts.

Recoveries (61 days or more) is not a negotiation band: there is no proposal and no promise. It is modelled as bands_outside -> event 'recoveries': say a colleague now handles the account (line recoveries_line), transfer to queue recoveries, and close as handed_over / recoveries.
'The Nth business day after today' counts from tomorrow and never includes today.

Ladder: attempt 1 is the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor on that day if the customer already said the full amount is too much (full_or_floor). Attempt 2, for the middle and late bands only, is the floor on the deadline. The early band uses attempt 1 only. The last step is not repeated, and a refused offer is never repeated.
The opening question 'Could you pay the full amount today?' is the first ask and is not a persuasion attempt (attempts are used only by a flat refusal or a non-answer).

The brief says to offer the floor once when the full amount is too much, and attempt 1 switches to the floor in that case. So the single floor offer is treated as attempt 1, on attempt 1's date (too_much_floor = attempt_1).
Rule 13: if a named date is a Sunday or holiday, offer the business day before it, or the first business day after it if that would be before today. So deadline_adjust is previous_business_day.
Refusing the deadline offer after a date past the deadline counts as a flat refusal (rule 14). A vague period gets one ask for an exact day, then the deadline is proposed.
Rule 25 says to say the confirmation letter sentence and then close as promised, so there is no 'anything else' turn (ask_anything_else false). The letter sentence is sms_line.

add_note has no product_id field in the API; its only fields are customer_id, reason (required) and text (optional free text). The engine requires a product slot, so n_product is mapped to the optional 'text' field (the product id is sent as free text), and n_reason to 'reason'. Notes are written only for rules 24, 26, 27 and 28 (system_fault, paid_claim, disputed, vulnerable). A refusal gets no note, and notes.enabled is false.

Hardship: one sentence of sympathy, no persuasion, add_note vulnerable, then a transfer to care, closing as handed_over / vulnerable. The brief does not ask for consent, so the hardship line says the transfer will happen.

A payment plan or lower repayments request goes to queue payment_plans (handed_over / restructure). A request for a person gets one 'can I help' ask first, then queue customer_desk (handed_over / agent_request).
Saying twice that they don't want to talk closes as no_commitment / declined (max_not_talk 2).
If create_promise fails, the engine retries once. If the second try also fails, it says the promise could not be recorded, writes add_note system_fault, and closes as no_commitment / system_error.
The brief has no rule for changing a promise, so the agent says it can't be changed on this call.
The brief has no wording for scam or robot questions, so the lines are generic and say nothing about the debt. id_failed refers the customer to the number on their card, as rule 8 requires.
The brief requires telling the customer the call is recorded. The opening says 'we record this call'.
All tool responses use the boolean 'ok' as the success flag.
